failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Answers exceeded the clue's requested scope, such as repeating supplied title wording, giving an exact year instead of a period, or returning a named instance rather than its class.

rejected_edits.content: When relevant snippets appear to conflict, assess which evidence best supports the full combination of clue details. Check whether apparent contradictions reflect different entities or timeframes before rejecting an otherwise well-supported candidate.

Treat grammatical relations as target cues: wording such as “this state's X” asks for the state, not X's divisions, members, or examples. Resolve pronouns and demonstratives to their referents, then identify the entity filling the requested possessive or relational slot. For example, if a clue says energy from “this” is measured by an instrument, “this” refers to the source, not the energy or radiation being measured or its measurement label.
rejected_edits.target: Treat grammatical relations as target cues: wording such as “this state's X” asks for the state, not X's divisions, members, or examples. Use context to identify the entity filling the possessive or relational slot.

rejected_edits.content: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer omitted wording when the clue explicitly asks for a completion. If the clue instead asks to identify a work or its title while giving only part of the title, return the full conventional title, not just the omitted word or supplied fragment.
rejected_edits.target: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer the omitted word or phrase that completes the clue rather than echoing the supplied text.
